claims.text: By default, flutter run compiles to debug mode; flutter run -d chrome therefore starts a debug build of the web app.
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: testing/build-modes.md#debug ('By default, flutter run compiles to debug mode')

claims.text: On the web, debug mode compiles with dartdevc, while release and profile modes compile with dart2js.
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: testing/build-modes.md (Debug/Release/Profile 'for a web app' lists)

claims.text: Debug mode enables extra checks (assertions) that do not run in profile or release, and is compiled for fast development cycles rather than execution speed; release is optimised for speed and size and strips debugging information.
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: testing/build-modes.md (Debug, Release); perf/ui-performance.md (Why you should run on a real device)

claims.text: Debug-mode performance is not indicative of release behaviour; performance should be measured in profile mode.
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: testing/build-modes.md (note: 'Application performance can be janky in debug mode'); perf/ui-performance.md (Connect to a physical device)

claims.text: Profile mode compiles almost identically to release mode but keeps enough functionality (tracing information) to debug performance; flutter run --profile compiles to profile mode.
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: perf/ui-performance.md (Run in profile mode); testing/build-modes.md#profile

claims.text: flutter build web builds release mode unless --profile or --debug is passed.
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: deployment/web.md (Building the app for release; Additional build flags); testing/build-modes.md#release

claims.text: At stage-2 scripts/up.sh runs flutter build web with no mode flag, then docker compose up; the app-web container serves DonHang.App/build/web on port 8081, printed as http://localhost:8081/.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: scripts/up.sh:8-22; docker-compose.yml app-web (volume ./DonHang.App/build/web, ports 8081:8081)

claims.text: To look smooth at 60 fps each frame must be ready in about 16 ms; frames that take longer are dropped, causing jank (a visible stutter).
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: perf/ui-performance.md ('each frame must render approximately every 16ms to avoid jank')

claims.text: In profile mode on the web, the framework's timeline events appear in the Chrome DevTools Performance panel recording; DevTools for Dart cannot connect to a profile-mode web app.
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: perf/web-performance.md (timeline events in Chrome DevTools performance panel; run in profile mode); testing/build-modes.md#profile

claims.text: The framework frame-phase timeline events are named BUILD, LAYOUT and PAINT (the root pipeline owner adds LAYOUT (root) and PAINT (root), with the plain ones nested inside), emitted only when !kReleaseMode, so a release build shows none.
claims.source_hint: Flutter SDK 3.47: widgets/framework.dart BuildOwner.buildScope (startSync('BUILD')); rendering/object.dart PipelineOwner.flushLayout/flushPaint ('LAYOUT', 'PAINT', inside if (!kReleaseMode))

claims.text: A low average frame time does not rule out jank: a few frames over budget among many fast ones still stutter.
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: perf/ui-performance.md ('if a frame occasionally takes 10 times longer than usual ... it will likely be dropped')

claims.text: When a change for speed makes code harder to read, make it only where a profile-mode recording shows a slow frame; a change that costs readability with no measured gain is a pure cost.
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: perf/best-practices.md (frames well under 16ms in profile mode: likely no need to worry); outline item 6

claims.text: Each slow phase (build, layout, paint) calls for a different kind of fix; for example, too much time in BUILD calls for rebuilding fewer widgets.
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: perf/best-practices.md (Avoid repetitive and costly work in build(); localize setState; saveLayer/opacity/clipping paint cost; intrinsic layout pass)

claims.text: On the web, you capture Flutter's timeline events by opening Chrome's developer tools, choosing the Performance panel and recording while you use the app; the recording holds the framework's entries for each frame.
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: perf/web-performance.md ('Open up the Chrome DevTools Performance panel ... start recording to capture timeline events'; run in profile mode)
